source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

36099.t:
Seneca County moved about 2 points toward the Republicans in the race for governor, going against the statewide shift. Blakeman beat Hochul here 6,623 to 5,021, a margin of 14 points, compared with Trump's 12-point win in 2024. Statewide, Hochul won by 20 points, a 7-point swing toward the Democrats from 2024. But New York's counties split almost evenly, and the typical one did not move. Nationally, nearly every counted county moved left, typically by 14 points.

Turnout fell to 78% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Comparable nearby counties also moved right, by more: Franklin 6 points, Madison and Cayuga 3 each.

36017.t:
In the race for New York governor, Chenango County moved 4 points toward the Republicans from the 2024 presidential vote, the opposite of the state's 7-point swing to the Democrats. Blakeman won the county 11,265 to 5,856 over Hochul, a 32-point margin, with 98% of the expected vote counted. Chenango ranked 51st of 62 New York counties by move, while the typical county in the state did not move at all and the typical county nationally moved 14 points left. Similar counties split: Montgomery and Schoharie moved about 3 points left, Tioga 2 points right.

Turnout was 17,159 votes, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

36089.t:
In the race for governor, St. Lawrence County moved about 7 points toward the Republicans, going from Trump's 18-point win in 2024 to a 25-point win for Blakeman over Hochul, 21,726 votes to 13,154. That runs against the state, which moved 7 points toward the Democrats as Hochul won by 20, and against the national pattern, where the typical county moved 14 points left. Only four of New York's 62 counties moved further right.

Turnout was 80% of the 2024 level, 34,944 votes against 43,929, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Chemung also moved right, by 9 points, while Sullivan and Greene moved left.

36093.t:
In the race for governor, Schenectady County gave Hochul (D) 31,799 votes to Blakeman's (R) 22,403, a 17-point Democratic margin. That is up from Harris's 11-point edge in 2024, a move of about 7 points toward the Democrats, roughly matching the state's shift. It ranks 11th of New York's 62 counties by move, where the typical county did not move at all. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Similar counties were mixed: Dutchess moved 7 points, Columbia 5 and Erie 1.

Only 54,365 votes were cast, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94.4% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

36087.t:
Rockland County swung hard toward the Democrats in the governor's race. Trump carried it by 12 points in 2024, but Hochul leads Blakeman here by 7, 63,962 votes to 55,726, a move of 19 points. That is the third-largest shift among New York's 62 counties, where the typical county did not move at all, and well above the national typical move of 14. Neighboring Orange moved almost as much (18 points), while Putnam moved 10 and Niagara stayed put.

Only about two-thirds of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 119,849 votes so far equal 80% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36061.t:
New York County held almost perfectly still in the race for governor. Hochul led Blakeman 397,886 to 85,117, a Democratic margin of 65 points, essentially matching Harris's 65-point margin over Trump in 2024; the shift was a fraction of a point toward the Republicans. That sets it apart from the state, which moved 7 points toward the Democrats, from similar counties such as Kings (15 points) and Bronx (21 points), and from the typical county nationally (14 points).

About 484,204 votes were counted, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 89% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

36085.t:

That is the sixth-largest shift toward the Democrats among New York's 62 counties, where the typical county did not move at all and the state as a whole moved 7 points. Comparable Republican-leaning counties went the other way or barely shifted: Steuben moved 5 points right and Montgomery 3 points left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 134,727 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

The move ranks 47th of New York's 62 counties. It is larger than in similar counties nearby, such as Chautauqua (2 points right), Livingston (1 point right) and Washington (no change). About 77,481 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36123.t:
In the governor's race, Yates County moved about 2 points toward the Republicans while New York as a whole swung 7 points toward the Democrats. Bruce Blakeman led Kathy Hochul 4,851 to 3,345, a margin of 18 points, up from Trump's 16-point margin over Harris in 2024. About 89% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move.

So far 8,196 votes have been cast, 78% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Yates ranks 41st of 62 New York counties by move. Among similar counties, Greene moved 5 points left and Sullivan 9, while Schuyler moved 6 right. Nationally, 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left.

36025.t:
In the race for governor, Delaware County went for Blakeman over Hochul by 21 points, 10,772 votes to 7,054. That is a 1-point shift toward the Republicans from Trump's 20-point win over Harris in 2024, while New York as a whole moved 7 points toward the Democrats. The county ranks 37th of 62 in the state by move. Half of New York's counties moved left, but the typical one did not move. Similar counties split: Livingston also moved 1 point right, Washington held steady, and Greene moved 5 points left.

About 17,871 votes have been counted, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

36013.t:
Chautauqua County moved slightly toward the Republicans in the race for governor, bucking New York's shift the other way. Blakeman beat Hochul here 26,355 to 16,278, a margin of 24 points, against Trump's 22-point win in 2024, a move of about 2 points to the right. Statewide, Hochul won by 20 points, 7 points better than Harris's margin, though the typical New York county barely moved. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points toward the Democrats.

Turnout fell to 75% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved little: Wayne held steady, while Oswego and Livingston each edged about 1 point rightward.

36113.t: Warren County voted for Bruce Blakeman, the Republican, over Kathy Hochul in the race for governor, 14,553 to 14,050, a margin of R+2. In 2024 Donald Trump carried it by 4 points, so the county moved under 3 points toward the Democrats. That is less than the state's 7-point shift and far below the typical national county move of 14 points, but it ranks 24th of 62 in New York, where the typical county did not move at all. Among similar counties, Cortland shifted slightly left, while Clinton and Otsego moved right. Turnout was 28,668 votes, 80% of 2024's 35,705, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

36115.t:
Washington County barely budged in the governor's race. Republican Bruce Blakeman beat Democrat Kathy Hochul here 13,667 to 8,901, a 21-point margin, essentially the same as Donald Trump's 21-point win in 2024. Hochul carried the state by 20 points, 7 points better than the Democrats' 2024 presidential result, but that shift did not reach this county.

Turnout fell to 22,620 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. The flat result matches the typical New York county, which also showed no net move. Similar counties such as Livingston, Delaware and Tioga moved 1 to 2 points toward the Republicans. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points toward the Democrats.

36059.t:
In the race for governor, Nassau County moved about 4 points toward the Democrats, from a 4-point Trump win in 2024 to a narrow Hochul edge over Blakeman: 266,444 votes to 265,277, a gap of 1,167. That makes it one of four New York counties to flip from Trump to the Democrat. With 98% of the expected vote counted, the result is close to final.

Its shift was smaller than the state's 7 points and well below the typical national move of 14, though larger than that of the typical New York county, which barely moved. Suffolk, similar in size, swung 11 points. Turnout was 532,336, or 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36047.t:
In the race for New York governor, Brooklyn's Democratic margin widened from 44 points for Harris in 2024 to 59 points for Hochul over Blakeman, a 15-point move toward the Democrats. That is double the statewide shift of 7 points and ranks fifth of 62 counties, while the typical New York county did not move at all. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points left. The Bronx moved further, 21 points, and Westchester moved 5.

Hochul leads 493,734 to 126,899, with 622,033 votes cast, the most of any county in the state. Only about 90% of the expected vote is counted, so these figures may still change. Turnout so far is 74% of 2024's, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

36019.t:
Clinton County moved against the grain in the governor's race. Trump carried it by 2 points in 2024; in 2026 Blakeman won it by nearly 10, 15,644 votes to 12,926 for Hochul, a shift of about 7 points toward the Republicans while the state as a whole moved 7 points toward the Democrats. Only two of New York's 62 counties moved further right, and nationally 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left.

Turnout was 80% of the 2024 vote, 28,610 ballots against 35,725, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Nearby comparisons were mixed: Essex also moved right, by 4 points, while Warren and Ontario edged left.

36069.t:
Ontario County barely shifted in the race for governor. Kathy Hochul, the Democrat, trailed Republican Bruce Blakeman here by less than a point, 23,590 votes to 23,330, a Republican margin of about 1 point. That is almost exactly where Harris finished against Trump in 2024, when she lost the county by 1 point. The move toward the Democrats was under 1 point, while the state as a whole moved 7 points their way and the typical county nationally moved 14.

Ontario's result sits in the middle of New York's 62 counties, close to the state's typical county, which did not move. Among similar counties, Clinton swung 7 points toward the Republicans, Broome held steady and Rensselaer moved 4 points toward the Democrats. Turnout was 79% of 2024's, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36007.t: In the governor's race between Hochul and Blakeman, Broome County stayed almost exactly where it was in 2024. Harris carried it by less than a point, and Hochul did the same, finishing 389 votes ahead, 34,292 to 33,903. The shift toward the Democrats rounds to zero, while the state as a whole moved 7 points their way and the typical county nationally moved 14. Broome's move matched the typical New York county and was smaller than those in similar counties such as Rensselaer (4 points) and Saratoga (3). About 68,333 votes were cast, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36051.t:
Livingston County moved about 1 point toward the Republicans in the race for governor, going from Trump's 21-point win in 2024 to Blakeman's 22-point margin over Hochul, 14,992 votes to 9,486. Hochul won the state by 20 points, a 7-point swing toward the Democrats from 2024.

The county's shift runs against the national pattern, where 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left and the typical one moved 14 points. In New York it was closer to the middle: 31 of 62 counties moved left, the typical one did not move at all, and Livingston ranks 36th. Similar counties did much the same. Washington was flat, while Tioga and Chautauqua each moved 2 points right. Turnout fell to 79% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

36055.t:
In the governor's race, Monroe County gave Hochul 167,229 votes to Blakeman's 104,824, a Democratic margin of 23 points. That is 4 points better for the Democrats than Harris's 19-point margin in 2024. The shift is smaller than the state's 7-point move toward Hochul but larger than that of the typical New York county, which did not move at all. Monroe ranks 19th of 62 counties by move. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

There were 272,802 votes cast, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties shifted by similar amounts: Onondaga by 2 points and Ulster by 6. Queens moved 20.

36035.t:
Fulton County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race, with Blakeman beating Hochul 12,173 votes to 6,175, a margin of 33 points. That is 3 points closer than Trump's 36-point win here in 2024. The shift was smaller than the state's 7-point swing toward the Democrats and far below the typical national county move of 14 points. It still ranks 20th of New York's 62 counties.

Similar counties went the other way: Herkimer, Genesee and Cattaraugus each moved 3 to 5 points toward the Republicans. Turnout in Fulton was 77% of the 2024 vote, with 18,379 ballots cast, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

36101.t:
In the race for New York governor, Steuben County moved toward Republican Bruce Blakeman even as Democrat Kathy Hochul won the state by 20 points. Blakeman carried the county 23,851 to 10,916, a 37-point margin, up from Trump's 32-point margin over Harris in 2024. That 5-point shift right ranks Steuben 55th of 62 New York counties. Statewide the race moved 7 points toward the Democrats, and nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 77% of the 2024 vote, 34,852 ballots against 45,190, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties split: Cattaraugus and Genesee also moved right, by 4 and 3 points, while Schoharie moved 3 points left.

36031.t:
Essex County went from a narrow Harris win in 2024, by less than a point, to a Republican win in the race for governor, with Blakeman beating Hochul 8,165 to 7,611, a margin of about 4 points. That is a shift of 4 points toward the Republicans, while the state as a whole moved 7 points toward the Democrats and the typical New York county did not move at all. Essex ranks 50th of 62 counties by move, and it is the only kind of flip the state saw in reverse: four counties went from Trump to the Democrats.

Turnout fell to 15,794 votes, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar Clinton County moved further right, by 7 points.
